title: Sancristóbal 2022 · Eyes-closed resting EEG
citation: Sancristóbal et al. (2022). Slow Resting State Fluctuations Enhance Neuronal and Behavioral Responses to Looming Sounds. Brain Topography, 35(1), 121–141.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.sequence: Day 2 starts with two 300 s eyes-closed resting recordings without task stimuli, followed by passive auditory EEG.
published_method.acquisition: Use a nominal 64-channel BrainAmp MR and synchronized Philips 3 T scanner at 5000 Hz. Reference FCz, ground Iz, and downsample to 500 Hz after removing gradient artifact.
published_method.scoring: Compute band-power autocorrelation in 20 s windows with 10 s overlap. Average autocorrelations within run, take the full width at half maximum and average across the two runs. Exclude channel-participant pairs if any spectral burst exceeds six IQR from the median.

implementation_gaps: Requires two stimulus-free timed recording runs with synchronized MR-compatible EEG and artifact monitoring.
The exact taper convention and software parameters, numerical cross-run exclusion threshold and original EEG inputs are unavailable.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
